# nginx-modules

Source bundles for [nginx_installer.sh](https://github.com/tmiland/nginx-installer). Version pins and source locations live here, not in the installer.

This repository ships source code, patches, and metadata only. It does not ship compiled nginx, Google PageSpeed Optimization Libraries (PSOL) binaries, or MaxMind GeoIP databases.

## Installer usage

Download a bundle from the latest release:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/tmiland/nginx-modules/releases/latest/download/nginx-modules-full.tar.gz
tar -xzf nginx-modules-full.tar.gz
cd nginx-modules-full
```

The archive root contains:

```text
modules/       module sources at their final directory names
versions.conf  version variables consumed by nginx_installer.sh
modules.conf   one module per line: id|dir|kind|build|requires|env
```

The installer parses `versions.conf`; do not source an untrusted copy. It contains the version variables for the modules in that archive; `legacy` and `candidate` entries are only present in bundles that include them. In `modules.conf`, `{dir}` is a placeholder for `modules/<dir>`:

```bash
MODULES_DIR=$PWD/modules
while IFS='|' read -r id dir kind build requires env; do
  [[ -z $id || $id == \#* ]] && continue
  printf '%s\n' "${build//\{dir\}/$MODULES_DIR/$dir}"
done < modules.conf
```

`build` is empty for libraries and patch files. Those entries need installer-side handling: build LuaJIT, libmaxminddb, ModSecurity, OpenSSL, or LibreSSL first; apply `kind = 'file'` patches to the nginx source tree.

The `full` bundle contains every `active` module. Named bundles are available for smaller source sets; build one with `bash scripts/build_bundle.sh --bundle <name>`. `legacy` or `candidate` modules are only included when explicitly selected.

## Bundles

`resolved` lists include dependencies pulled in through `requires`.
Bundle files themselves list only directly selected modules.

| Bundle | Name | Description | Resolved modules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core` | [Core](bundles/core.bundle) | Common HTTP performance and content-filtering modules. | `brotli`, `headers-more`, `fancyindex`, `cachepurge`, `subfilter` |
| `http3` | [HTTP/3](bundles/http3.bundle) | quiche with the TLS dynamic-record, HTTP/3, and HPACK patches. | `quiche`, `tlsdyn`, `http3`, `hpack`, `hpack-http3` |
| `legacy` | [Legacy](bundles/legacy.bundle) | Unmaintained PageSpeed module sources. The PSOL binary is not bundled. | `pagespeed` |
| `lua` | [Lua](bundles/lua.bundle) | LuaJIT, ngx_devel_kit, lua-nginx-module, the OpenResty Lua libraries, and set-misc. | `luajit2`, `ngx-devel-kit`, `lua-nginx`, `lua-resty-core`, `lua-resty-lrucache`, `set-misc` |
| `media` | [Media](bundles/media.bundle) | nginx-rtmp-module for RTMP streaming. | `rtmp` |
| `observability` | [Observability](bundles/observability.bundle) | nginx-module-vts for virtual-host traffic statistics. | `vts` |
| `security` | [Security](bundles/security.bundle) | ModSecurity v3 with its nginx connector and the testcookie challenge module. | `modsecurity`, `modsecurity-nginx`, `testcookie` |
| `web` | [Web](bundles/web.bundle) | Core modules plus Redis, cache, echo, and statistics helpers. | `brotli`, `headers-more`, `fancyindex`, `cachepurge`, `subfilter`, `echo`, `ngx-devel-kit` (dep), `set-misc`, `srcache`, `redis2`, `httpredis`, `vts` |
| `full` | Full (auto) | All active modules plus their required dependencies. | `brotli`, `cachepurge`, `echo`, `fancyindex`, `libmaxminddb`, `geoip2`, `headers-more`, `hpack`, `hpack-http3`, `http3`, `httpredis`, `libressl`, `luajit2`, `ngx-devel-kit`, `lua-nginx`, `lua-resty-core`, `lua-resty-lrucache`, `modsecurity`, `modsecurity-nginx`, `openssl`, `quiche`, `redis2`, `rtmp`, `set-misc`, `srcache`, `subfilter`, `testcookie`, `tlsdyn`, `vts`, `webdav`, `zstd` |

## Updating pins

1. Edit the relevant `modules/<id>.mod` file.
2. Run `python3 scripts/build_catalog.py` to refresh the JSON catalog and this README.
3. Run `bash scripts/update-modules.sh --check` to look for upstream drift.

Git modules are pinned to full commit SHAs. Archive modules are pinned to tags or release versions; add a `sha256` when a stable checksum is available. Patch files always carry a checksum.
